title: Foreign residents capital gains withholding variations

sections.heading: Foreign residents selling Australian property
sections.text:
Foreign residents (also known as non-residents) are subject to the full rate of foreign resident capital gains withholding (FRCGW).

FRCGW is applied to the sale price (or market value if non-arm's length) when selling Australian real property (property), unless there is a variation notice that reduces the rate.

A foreign resident may claim a credit for the withheld FRCGW by declaring the capital gain (or loss) and lodging a tax return at the end of the income year the sale contract was signed. They may receive a refund if the FRCGW amount exceeds the amount of tax payable on their tax assessment.

sections.heading: Rate of withholding from a property sale
sections.text:
The following FRCGW rates apply to the market value of property contracts signed:

- From 1 January 2025, a rate of 15% applies to the value of all property.
- From 1 July 2017 to 31 December 2024, a rate of 12.5% applies to property valued at $750,000 or more.
- From 1 July 2016 to 30 June 2017, a rate of 10% applies to real property valued at $2,000,000 and above.

sections.heading: When to apply for a variation notice
sections.text:
Vendors can apply for a variation to the FRCGW rate when **both** the following apply:

- they're not entitled to a clearance certificate
- the rate of 15% is too high when considering their estimated Australian tax liability on the sale of the asset.

Reasons why **foreign residents** may apply for a variation include:

- there's no capital gain on the transaction (for example, because of a capital loss or a CGT roll-over)
- there is a reduced income tax liability, or tax losses (for example, capital losses can be used to reduce any capital gains) and a rate between 0% and 15% is applicable.

Reasons why **Australian residents** (who may not be the vendor) can apply for a variation include:

- the property is being sold because of a Family Law settlement to a third party
- a creditor of the vendor has a mortgage or other security interest over the property and the proceeds of the sale at settlement won't cover the amount to be withheld and discharge the debt the property secures
- a creditor acquires legal title to the property (becomes the purchaser) due to foreclosure and its security would be reduced by withholding.

Purchasers must withhold the full rate of FRCGW when there's no clearance certificate or variation provided to them at or before settlement.

For more detail, see LI 2026/38 Taxation Administration (PAYG Withholding Variation for Foreign Resident Capital Gains Withholding Payments) Legislative Instrument 2026.

sections.heading: When to apply for a variation notice > Foreign residents and the main residence exemption
sections.text: Foreign residents can't claim the CGT main residence exemption, unless the life events test applies.

sections.heading: When to apply for a variation notice > Mortgagee sales
sections.text:
Where the mortgagee exercises their right to the sale of the property they can apply for a variation. This is where the proceeds from the sale of the property will not cover the liability where the FRCGW amount is required to be paid; see Mortgagee sales.

If you are an Australian deposit-taking institution (such as an Australian bank), in some circumstances, the rate of withholding is varied to 0%. For more detail, see LI 2026/38.

sections.heading: Apply for a variation
sections.text:
Variations take up to **28 days** to process.

To be eligible for a variation, foreign residents (where applicable) need all Australian tax affairs up to date. This means:

- if the property was used to generate income, you must lodge an income tax return declaring your rental income; all due tax returns must be lodged
- you have paid all due tax debts with the ATO.

To apply for a variation of the withholding rate:

1. Lodge an application as soon as the contract is signed.
2. You **must** include the sales contract with the application (and purchase contract if available).
3. You should also include with the application

- a statement showing your calculations and how you calculated your new withholding rate
- other relevant documentation relating to your application

- if a deceased estate, a copy of the will, death certificate and probate documents if applicable
- any Family law court documents showing the property transfer judgment, see Relationship breakdown.
4. Wait for your variation notice to be issued.
5. Provide the variation notice to the purchaser at or **before** settlement to ensure the reduced withholding rate applies.

When multiple vendors own a property, each vendor needs to apply for their own variation.

Apply for a variation
For help, see instructions to complete an application for a variation.

A paper application and instructions are also available. See Foreign resident capital gains withholding rate variation paper application.

sections.heading: Apply for a variation > Who can apply
sections.text:
Those who can apply for a variation notice include:

- vendors
- Australian legal practitioners and registered tax agents representing the vendor on their behalf
- creditors who are owed a debt payable by a vendor
- purchasers.

Conveyancers should advise each vendor to apply for their own online variation notice themselves, or to seek professional legal and tax advice.

sections.heading: Apply for a variation > Receiving your notice of variation
sections.text:
Variation notices are sent to the email address provided in the application or, if there's no email address, mailed to the vendor and the applicant's addresses provided.

If you choose to communicate with us via email, be aware the internet isn't a secure environment. We can't guarantee the privacy and security of personal information.

sections.heading: Calculate a reduced rate of withholding
sections.text:
The varied withholding rate we approve depends on the information provided in the application.

Vendors can calculate the reduced rate of withholding that should apply to them based on their information.

It's the vendor’s responsibility to give the purchaser a valid variation notice by the settlement date.

Refer to cost base of assets to help work out any capital gains or losses.

sections.heading: Multiple vendors
sections.text:
If there are multiple vendors selling or disposing of a property, each vendor has a responsibility to provide their own clearance certificate or variation depending on their tax residency.

See multiple vendor examples to determine how much withholding would apply in different circumstances.

sections.heading: Foreign resident tax returns
sections.text:
Foreign residents may need to apply for a tax file number (TFN) before lodging an income tax return with us.

To claim a credit for the FRCGW amount, the vendor must have a copy of the Payment Confirmation from the purchaser.

When completing a tax return:

- declare assessable income, including any capital gain or loss from the disposal of the asset
- claim the amount withheld from sale proceeds as a **Credit for foreign resident capital gains withholding amounts** at the correct label, (unlike other withholding credits, this amount is not pre-filled).

The FRCGW amount will be refunded in full if there's no:

- tax debts
- CGT payable on the sale of the property
- tax payable on any other Australian sourced income.

The income year of the tax return is the year the sale contract was signed (not the date of settlement).

A credit for the amount withheld for FRCGW applies to the income year the contract was signed. It may take time before the foreign resident can lodge their tax return to declare the capital gain and claim any credit for the amount withheld. This is generally because tax returns can't be lodged before the end of the relevant income year. Any amount due will be refunded after the tax return is assessed.

If the contract is signed in one income year but the purchaser pays the FRCGW in the next income year, the capital gain and claim for the credit for FRCGW amounts should be included in the income year the sale contract was signed.

In certain circumstances, an early tax return may be lodged with us. If a foreign resident vendor isn't eligible to lodge an early tax return, they must wait until the end of the income year.

The credit can only be applied to the vendor for whom the amount was withheld. If the vendor is a trust, the credit can only be applied to the relevant beneficiary. Credits are allocated according to each vendor's legal interest in the asset at the time of disposal.

The allocation of credits can't be adjusted because of:

- court orders or other arrangements affecting how sale proceeds are distributed after settlement
- events that occur after the disposal of the asset.
